name: Psychology
school: College of Literature, Science, and the Arts

requirements.label: 120 Total Credits
requirements.hint: All credits completed at U-M plus posted transfer credit.

requirements.label: 100 LSA Credits
requirements.hint: Credits from courses recognized by LSA (most U-M courses except some SI offerings and other school-specific courses).

requirements.label: 60 BS-Eligible Credits (for BS students only)
requirements.hint: Only counts for students pursuing a Bachelor of Science.

requirements.label: 90 Credits Excluding Experiential and Independent Study Courses
requirements.hint: At least 90 credits must come from standard coursework; internships and independent study don't count.

requirements.label: 60 Credits outside Psychology
requirements.hint: Credits earned in courses outside the Psychology department(s).

requirements.label: 90 Credits of Graded Course Work, Including Transfer and Test
requirements.hint: At least 90 credits must carry a letter grade (transfer and test credit included).

requirements.label: 60 Credits of In-Residence Course Work (AA Campus and U-M Study Abroad)
requirements.hint: Credits taken on the Ann Arbor campus or through an approved U-M study abroad program.

requirements.label: 30 Credits Taken While Enrolled in LSA
requirements.hint: Credits earned while officially enrolled in LSA (as opposed to another U-M college).

requirements.label: First Year Writing Requirement
requirements.hint: one course required

requirements.label: Upper Level Writing Requirement
requirements.hint: one course required

requirements.label: Race and Ethnicity Requirement
requirements.hint: one course required

requirements.label: Quantitative Reasoning Requirement
requirements.hint: 1 QR1 or 2 QR2 courses required

requirements.label: Language Requirement
requirements.hint: one 4th term course required, C- minimum, or one course where proficiency is presumed

requirements.label: Area Distribution: 7 Credits in Humanities
requirements.hint: From approved HU-designated courses.

requirements.label: Area Distribution: 7 Credits in Natural Sciences
requirements.hint: From approved NS-designated courses.

requirements.label: Area Distribution: 7 Credits in Social Sciences
requirements.hint: From approved SS-designated courses.

requirements.label: Additional Distribution: complete 3 areas
requirements.hint: Pick any 3 of the area buckets below and hit 3 cr in each. ID credit can count toward 1, 2, or all 3 areas, so the extra ID buckets can stand in for additional areas.

requirements.label: Additional 3 Credits in Humanities
requirements.hint: Beyond the initial 7 cr Humanities.

requirements.label: Additional 3 Credits in Natural Sciences
requirements.hint: Beyond the initial 7 cr Natural Sciences.

requirements.label: Additional 3 Credits in Social Sciences
requirements.hint: Beyond the initial 7 cr Social Sciences.

requirements.label: 3 Credits in Mathematical & Symbolic Analysis
requirements.hint: From approved MSA-designated courses.

requirements.label: 3 Credits in Creative Expression
requirements.hint: From approved CE-designated courses.

requirements.label: 3 Credits in Interdisciplinary
requirements.hint: From approved ID-designated courses. ID credit can count toward 1, 2, or all 3 areas.

requirements.label: 3 Additional Credits in Interdisciplinary (Second Area)
requirements.hint: A second 3 cr of ID credit may stand in for a second area.

requirements.label: 3 Additional Credits in Interdisciplinary (Third Area)
requirements.hint: A third 3 cr of ID credit may stand in for a third area.

requirements.label: Introductory Course
requirements.hint: Choose 1 of: PSYCH 111, PSYCH 112, or PSYCH 114. C or better.

requirements.label: Statistics
requirements.hint: Choose 1 of: DATASCI 101, STATS 250, or STATS 280. C- or better.

requirements.label: Breadth Group I
requirements.hint: Choose 1 of: PSYCH 220, PSYCH 235, or PSYCH 240.

requirements.label: Breadth Group II
requirements.hint: Choose 1 of: PSYCH 250 or PSYCH 270.

requirements.label: Breadth Group III
requirements.hint: Choose 1 of: PSYCH 280, PSYCH 290, or PSYCH 291.

requirements.label: Methods-Based Lab: 3 Credits
requirements.hint: One methods-based lab of at least 3 credits taken in a single term, per the Methods-Based Labs list on the department's Psychology Major Worksheet (effective Fall 2021 to present, updated 2/18/2025). PSYCH 426 and 429 from the thesis sequence also fulfill the methods lab.

requirements.label: Additional Methods-Based or Experiential Lab: 3 Credits
requirements.hint: One more lab of at least 3 credits taken in a single term: either a second methods-based lab or an experiential lab (community-based or research-based), per the lab lists on the department's Psychology Major Worksheet (updated 2/18/2025). PSYCH 424 and 428 from the thesis sequence count as the experiential lab, and the department's Fall 2026 course chart also counts PSYCH 409 as an experiential lab. Labs graded credit/no credit satisfy this category but do not add to the 32 major credits.

requirements.label: Upper-Level Electives: 12 Credits
requirements.hint: 4 courses and 12 credits of lecture or seminar-based PSYCH courses at the 300 level or above (the 4 courses are broken out below).

requirements.label: 300-Level Electives: 2 Courses
requirements.hint: 2 lecture or seminar-based 300-level PSYCH courses that the department designates Upper Level Elective on its term course charts (union of the published Spring/Summer 2025, Spring/Summer 2026, and Fall 2026 charts). COGSCI 200 or PSYCH 225 can be substituted for 1 of the 2 courses.

requirements.label: 400-Level Elective: 1 Course
requirements.hint: 1 lecture or seminar-based 400-level PSYCH course that the department designates Upper Level Elective on its term course charts (union of the published Spring/Summer 2025, Spring/Summer 2026, and Fall 2026 charts). Per the department worksheet, PSYCH 420 and 421 cannot be your only 400-level course and are not on the charts' elective list.

requirements.label: Additional 300-Level or Above Elective: 1 Course
requirements.hint: 1 more lecture or seminar-based PSYCH course at the 300 level or above that the department designates Upper Level Elective on its term course charts (union of the published Spring/Summer 2025, Spring/Summer 2026, and Fall 2026 charts). No 200-level substitutions allowed.

requirements.label: Major Total Credits: minimum 32
requirements.hint: Includes all courses used toward the major requirements, including those from other departments. Does not include prerequisites or courses graded credit/no credit. If needed, an additional elective can be used to reach 32 credits. The introductory and statistics prerequisites are excluded from this count; COGSCI 200 and other approved substitutions are included.

requirements.label: Upper-Level Residency Requirement: minimum 12 credits
requirements.hint: Minimum 12 upper-level credits must be completed in-residence (AA Campus Department of Psychology and U-M Study Abroad).

requirements.label: Residency Requirement: minimum 24 credits
requirements.hint: Minimum 24 credits (can include the introductory PSYCH course) must be completed in-residence (AA Campus Department of Psychology and U-M Study Abroad).
